requested.title: Password confirmation is not enforced by the server-side schema
deleteTodo reports success when no row was deleted

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: The finding described a real server-side validation gap, but the current `src/schemas/user-schemas.ts` now applies an object-level `.refine(data => data.password === data.passwordConfirmation)` to `updateUserSchema`. Because `src/server/handlers/user-handlers.ts` registers that schema with `.validator(updateUserSchema)`, mismatched values are rejected before the handler reaches `auth.api.changePassword`. This also rejects a non-empty password with an omitted confirmation, since the confirmation defaults to an empty string and therefore fails equality. The handler still uses only `data.password` as the new password, but that is safe with respect to this contract because schema validation has already established that it matches the confirmation. Authentication and current-password verification remain additional protections, although they did not themselves mitigate the original contract bug. The same equality refinement has also been added to `signUpSchema`. Tests in `src/schemas/user-schemas.test.ts` explicitly cover rejection of mismatched signup and profile passwords. The repository HEAD is commit `a041f94337e958247fb48f6d2ab0ed41cb6dc446` (`Harden session and profile data handling`), and the current refinement constitutes the recommended patch.

The original logic bug was valid because checking the truthiness of Drizzle's returned array would not distinguish an empty result from a successful deletion. In the current `src/server/services/todo-service.ts`, however, the result is destructured with `const [todo] = await db.delete(...).returning()`. If the compound `id` and `userId` predicate matches no row, destructuring yields `undefined`, so `if (!todo)` now throws `new AppError("NOT_FOUND")` rather than returning success. The end-to-end handler validates the identifier as a UUID and obtains the authenticated user through `useLoggedInAppSession`, while the service's ownership predicate continues to prevent cross-user deletion. Consequently, a nonexistent, stale, or another user's todo ID can no longer produce `{ success: true }`. Tests in `src/server/services/todo-service.server.test.ts` now assert `NOT_FOUND` for both a nonexistent todo and another user's todo, while also confirming that the other user's row remains intact. The repository HEAD is commit `a041f94337e958247fb48f6d2ab0ed41cb6dc446` (`Harden session and profile data handling`), and the current destructuring exactly implements the recommended fix.
